'''Inamul Haque''' ([[Assamese language|Assamese]]: ইনামুল হক) (1 March 1940&nbsp;– 2 February 2014) was an eminent Indian-born [[Lecturer]] in [[Chemistry]]. He was a great visionary as well as a dedicated teacher of Chemistry in [[Assam]].  He died on 2 February 2014.

==Early life==
Inamul Haque was born in a small village of Murabazar of [[Sivasagar]], [[Assam]], [[India]].{{cn|date=October 2024}}

==Career==
He started his career as a lecturer at [[Cotton College, Guwahati|Cotton College]] in 1963. Then he joined [[Sibsagar College]] (1963&nbsp;– 65) from where he went to [[Imperial College London]] (1965&nbsp;– 68) to pursue research work. He worked on [[Spectroscopy]] and was awarded [[PhD]] degree by [[London University]] in 1968.{{cn|date=October 2024}}

After returning from abroad, he joined [[Dibrugarh University]] and retired from there in 2003. During his stay at [[Dibrugarh University]], he produced 15 [[PhD]]s under him and published 45 scientific papers in reputed [[Academic journal|journals]].{{cn|date=October 2024}} He was entrusted with the responsibility of being a member of the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, PG Board and UG Board of [[Dibrugarh University]].{{cn|date=October 2024}} He also acted as a [[Vice Chancellor]] of [[Dibrugarh University]] for a brief period.<ref>[http://www.cottoncollege.org.in/index_page.asp?slno=59 A collection of life sketches of more than 200 past teachers of Cotton College, Assam]. Published by Tarakeswar Choudhury, President, Cotton College Retired Teacher's Forum in May 2011</ref>

==Life at Salt Brook Academy==
After his retirement he joined [[Salt Brook Academy]], Dibrugarh, Assam as a [[Rector (academia)|Rector]].{{cn|date=October 2024}} He devoted his retired life to teach young students to build their future. He was a source of inspiration to every student of Salt Brook Academy. He taught [[Chemistry]] there.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sentinelassam.com/sunday/melange_cover_story.php?sec=7&subsec=0&ppr=2&dtP=2012-06-15 |title="&#91;&#91;Aswini Dowerah&#93;&#93;, Director of Saltbrook Academy, recalled the idea behind the inception of the institution"-The Sentinel. Retrieved 15 June 2012 |access-date=25 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924101404/http://www.sentinelassam.com/sunday/melange_cover_story.php?sec=7&subsec=0&ppr=2&dtP=2012-06-15 |archive-date=24 September 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>{{bcn|date=October 2024}}
[[File:Group Photo 2011.JPG|thumb|Annual group photo with faculties of Salt Brook Academy, 2011]]

==Death==
During his tenure as a [[Rector (academia)|Rector]] at Salt Brook Academy he succumbed to [[cancer]]. On 2 February 2014 he took his last breath.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://saltbrookacademy.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=101&Itemid=497 |title=Director's Message Salt Brook Academy. Retrieved June 2015 |access-date=25 July 2015 |archive-date=3 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203222402/http://saltbrookacademy.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=101&Itemid=497 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
